title: A photon loses energy but momentum still balances
promptMarkdown: A photon of energy $E=m_ec^2$ along $+x$ scatters from a free electron initially at rest. The outgoing photon is rotated counterclockwise by $60^\circ$ from $+x$ toward $+y$ in the xy plane. Derive its energy from four-momentum conservation. Find the recoil electron's kinetic energy, momentum components, speed and direction. Verify its mass shell and explain why equating photon energy loss to electron rest energy would fail.
hintLadder: Square $p+k-k\prime$ and use the unchanged electron mass.
Subtract momentum vectors component by component.
Use the recoil total energy in $\mathbf v=c^2\mathbf p/E_e$.

criteria.criterion: Photon energy follows from the recoil mass shell.
